title: Labelle Toda numerator unimodality
source: Antoine Labelle, On a specialization of Toda eigenfunctions, arXiv:2502.10655v3 (28 July 2026), Definition 1.1, Theorem 1.1, Conjecture 7.3. https://arxiv.org/html/2502.10655v3
source_open_excerpt: Paraphrase: multiplying the specialized Toda rational function by the square of its root-indexed q-factorial is conjectured always to produce a unimodal polynomial.
source_paper_text: Operator editorial formalization. Choose any finite reduced crystallographic root system with simple roots alpha_1,...,alpha_l and invariant positive-definite form normalized so short roots have squared length2 (componentwise for a semisimple root system). Let d_i=(alpha_i,alpha_i)/2. For a nonnegative integer vector a define alpha=sum_i a_i alpha_i and (q)_a=product_i product_{j=1}^{a_i}(1-q^(d_i*j)). Set J_0(q)=1 and, for a nonzero, J_a(q)=[1-q^((alpha,alpha)/2)]^(-1) * sum_{0<=b<=a,b!=a} q^((beta,beta)/2) J_b(q)/(q)_(a-b), where beta=sum_i b_i alpha_i and inequalities on vectors are coordinatewise. This finite recursion uniquely defines rational functions. Theorem1.1 establishes H_a(q)=(q)_a^2 J_a(q) in Z[q]. Conjecture7.3 asserts H_a is unimodal for EVERY such root system and vector a. Unimodality concerns all consecutive exponents of q, including zero coefficients: some peak separates weak increase from weak decrease. The source proves positivity in type A and special cases; it does not settle this full unimodality assertion. A refutation must give the root system or exact Gram matrix, a, and the exact polynomial computed from the recursion.
target: Settle the full original conjecture, prioritizing discovery of a finite counterexample. For REFUTED provide exact witness data, a proof that every hypothesis holds, and a reproducible exact certificate of the failed conclusion. Numerical approximations alone are insufficient. A valid universal proof is PROVED, not REFUTED; finite passing searches are only partial progress.
